text:
maria: Heads-up — I opened a follow-up after the Architecture RFC about long-lived tech debt tranches. Want to align on rollback criteria and feedback loops before Q3 planning.

akshay: Thanks — can you paste the short proposal? I only skimmed the RFC.

maria: Copied below: 3-tier debt tranching (hot, warm, cold); ownership deadlines; automatic telemetry gates; and canary rollback rules. Key ask: agree on metrics and signal owners.

jordan: Where do we store the tranche ledger? A simple GH doc or infra-backed tracking service?

sasha: Recommend infra-backed (internal "debt-registry") — we tried GH doc last time and it drifted. Will need small schema: tranche id, owner, SLA impact, estimated effort, last touch.

dominik: Agree infra-backed. Also need per-tranche CI checks: e.g., if tranche is >30d without action, send to oncall and escalate.

maria: Escalation cadence sounds good. For metrics, propose: open PR count touching tranche, avg latency regressions by service, and blocked customer incidents attributed. Thoughts?

akshay: :thumbsup: Those sound measurable. Also add 'deployment rollbacks per service' as a proxy for instability.

jordan: How do we prevent gaming metrics? Teams might close PRs without fixing. Need quality check: prompt-level evals? or qa signoff?

sasha: Maybe require 1 autograde check tied to eval harness + one manual reviewer before tranche can be marked "addressed."

dominik: Operationally, can we attach a 'tranche' label to GH issues and enforce checks via our GH app? Minimal infra work.

maria: Plan: build a thin 'tranche' registry, GH label + webhook integrated, dashboards in Console. Rollout: pilot w/ 'serving-runtime' and 'kv-cache' teams.

akshay: What about rollback criteria for API / model-serving changes? I propose: any canary with latency tail >2x baseline for 10m -> automatic rollback; error rate >1% for 5m -> roll back.

sasha: Need to ensure canary windows don't trigger false positives during traffic spikes. Use smoothed metrics and compare to baseline percentiles.

jordan: Agree. Also add 'graceful degrade' policy where fallback model variant is used instead of full rollback for certain customer tiers.

dominik: Who owns the rollback automation? Eng-sre or runtime?

maria: SRE owns automation; runtime defines safe fallbacks. We'll document fallbacks per service in the registry.

akshay: Timeline? Q2 pilot, Q3 org-wide adoption?

maria: Yes. Action items: Sasha to draft registry schema; Dominik to spike GH app for labels; Akshay + Jordan to define canary guardrails; Maria to prep pilot onboarding doc.

sasha: I'll post a PR by EOD Fri with schema draft.

dominik: I'll start a spike branch; will need 2 days.

jordan: I'll collect baseline percentile numbers for the next two services.

akshay: I'll write up canary guardrail doc and add to runbook.

maria: Thanks. Quick Q: @oncall-bot, can you add a weekly reminder for tranche review channel (#eng-debt-review) starting next Monday?

oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: weekly @eng-debt-review every Monday 10:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:

sasha: :tada: Nice. One more: add a field in the registry for 'rollback-mode' (full rollback, degrade-to-variant, throttle).

maria: Done. Ok team — let's reconvene in two weeks for pilot status. :calendar:
